cases.prompt: Create a Surface Contact Viewer at /contacts. Define a contact with string id and name, optional string email, and Boolean active fields. Look it up by string id. Describe an interface that asks for an id, displays name, email, and active status, and explains missing-input and not-found behavior. Also describe / as a non-visual screen that should redirect to /contacts.
acceptance: The result is valid Surface 0.1 KDL with exactly one application and at least one screen.
The contact fields use only (string) and (boolean) node annotations; only email has bare optional.
The query declares and inputs a private lookup entity and returns the global contact through typed references.
The query context says that no match returns null.
A top-level interface contains only contexts that reference the query and entity and describe the requested UI behavior.
The /contacts screen uses the interface with use (interface), and all references resolve.
A context-only / screen describes the redirect with a checked (screen) reference.
No section, title, text, UI field, state, logic, or redirect node is introduced.

cases.prompt: Starting from examples/03-contact-viewer/surface.kdl, add an optional string phone field to the Contact Viewer entity and update its interface intent so phone is displayed after email. Preserve comments, existing context, query structure, screens, and unrelated content.
acceptance: The entity adds exactly one (string) phone field with the bare optional modifier after email.
The interface context is minimally updated to display phone after email without adding structured UI nodes.
The query, screens, comments, existing context, and unrelated content are preserved.
The result remains valid Surface 0.1 KDL.

cases.prompt: Diagnose a Contact Viewer whose id field uses the unsupported required modifier, whose returns value omits the entity annotation, whose private entity shadows a global entity, whose input references an undeclared entity, whose screen uses a query instead of an interface, and whose interface contains a section child.
acceptance: The response identifies all six Surface validation problems.
It explains that use requires a checked interface reference and interfaces accept only context children.
The response distinguishes valid KDL from valid Surface.
Every suggested correction uses only released syntax.
